serviceReports.faultFound:
During the initial visit, the troubleshooting system identified insufficient power, with only 17VDC at the switches. Additional power supplies were necessary due to the new blind relay units added to the system. 

The operating voltage needed to exceed 20VDC for proper functionality, so three extra power supplies were installed, one on each floor, to ensure the system operated adequately.

Programming for Levels 3, 4, and 5 was required. The first visit focused on Level 3, where I was informed that I would need to reprogram all switches and relays to accommodate the room changes. The rooms had been divided from one large space into separate areas. 

During this process, I encountered programming anomalies, such as duplicate addressing and minor persistent bugs, which I was able to fix and resolve. Some motors were also found to be driving in the wrong directions, but these will be corrected. Initially, I had difficulty matching the relays to their corresponding rooms, blinds, shades, and switches.

Nick (Blinds Quickly) and the electrician were scheduled to return to help identify which motors were linked to which rooms.

serviceReports.faultFound:
The client reported several issues, including button presses not registering, lights flickering or turning off and on during bad weather, and lights turning on and requiring multiple resets throughout the day and night. These symptoms are typically associated with faulty internal power supply issues, which are beginning to fail due to age. The affected units are dated from 2006/7, and the internal components are approaching the end of their lifecycle.

Additionally, it was found that the Reflection Series switches are outdated and deteriorating, with magnetic fascias failing and buttons missing.
serviceReports.workPerformed: Identified and scanned C-Bus system at above address, found system to be in ok condition, units scanned and identified.
serviceReports.recommendations:
Based on the faults reported and the condition of the existing equipment, it is recommended that the current C-Bus relay units and wall switches be upgraded to improve system reliability, functionality, and long-term serviceability.

The existing relay units installed on site are dated from approximately 2006–2007 and are approaching the end of their operational lifecycle. The issues experienced—including intermittent button response, lights flickering during adverse weather conditions, and lighting circuits switching on and off unexpectedly—are consistent with age-related internal power supply degradation, which is a known failure point in older relay hardware. As these components continue to age, faults are expected to become more frequent and may ultimately result in complete relay failure.

To rectify this, the existing relay units should be replaced with the Schneider Electric SpaceLogic C-Bus Relay series. These newer generation relays feature improved internal power supplies, updated electronics, and enhanced reliability while remaining fully compatible with the existing C-Bus infrastructure.

When installed, the new relay units will also provide additional spare channels beyond the current requirements, allowing for future expansion should additional lighting circuits or loads need to be integrated into the system without requiring further relay hardware replacement.

During inspection it was also identified that the existing Reflection Series wall switches are now outdated and deteriorating, with several magnetic fascias failing and buttons missing. These switches should be replaced with modern C-Bus smart wall switches.

Both the single, two-gang and four-gang C-Bus switches, as well as the digital series switches, incorporate advanced scene control functionality. This allows multiple lighting groups to be controlled from a single button press, enabling preset lighting scenes such as entertaining, evening, or pathway lighting to be activated instantly.

The digital series switches provide even greater flexibility by supporting multiple pages of control, with up to 16 pages of configurable functions per switch. This allows a single switch location to control numerous lighting groups, scenes, or automation functions throughout the property.

Together, these upgrades ensure the system is fitted with the latest generation C-Bus technology, providing improved reliability, enhanced user control, and significant capacity for future programming, automation features, or system expansion without requiring further hardware replacement.

Upgrading both the relay units and wall switches will modernise the existing C-Bus installation, resolve the current reliability issues, and provide a stable, flexible lighting control platform designed to support the property well into the future.

serviceReports.workPerformed:
Site Attendance Report – C-Bus Lighting System

Site: Western Sydney University Campbelltown Campus/ Building 30
Date: Monday, 30 March 2026
System: Clipsal C-Bus

Attendance Summary

Attended site to investigate issue with external lighting not switching ON for the North and South external light poles.

Inspected multiple C-Bus distribution boards across Ground Level and Level 1 and scanned C-Bus networks to locate relay control units, PE Cells, schedules and application controllers.

Findings
Ground Level – Northern Lighting (DB GP2)
Scanned C-Bus network and located relay units controlling the northern external lighting.
No PE Cell present in this board.
It was advised that the PE Cell for the northern lights should be fed from DB GP2, however none was found connected at this board.
Ground Level – Southern Lighting (DB GP3)
Located PE Cell connected to southern lighting control network.
Network scan confirmed this board was controlling the southern external light poles.
PE Cell Inspection

Using a scissor lift, both PE Cells were physically inspected.

Northern PE Cell
Broken wire found.
Wire was repaired and re-terminated.
Voltage measured at approximately 30V DC present.
PE Cell covered to simulate night conditions.
Lighting did not switch ON.
Southern PE Cell
Voltage present.
PE Cell covered to simulate night conditions.
Lighting did not switch ON.
Lux Level Adjustment
Attempted adjustment of PE Cell lux levels.
Still unable to trigger lighting ON.
Level 1 Boards – Schedule / Logic Check
Located PAC (Programmable Automation Controller).
This PAC was found to be only controlling theatre lighting.
No external lighting schedules found in this controller.
Network Bridge / Application Controller Investigation
Connected to network bridge in southern board.
Discovered additional network containing 5500AC2 Application Controller located in LAB building board.
Attempted connection but unit was password protected.
Contacted mySmart, however password was not available.
Advised that a Head End PC was located on Level 2.
Head End PC / Schedule Plus
Located head end PC running Schedule Plus.
External lighting schedules were found.
Adjusted system time to current time to test schedule activation.
Schedules did not activate lighting.
Possible Causes

Lighting control issue may be caused by one or more of the following:

Network bridge communication failure / freeze
Incorrect or corrupted programming in Application Controller
Broken or disconnected C-Bus network cabling
Schedule Plus not communicating with network
serviceReports.faultFound:
Issues Identified
PE Cells Non-Operational
Both northern and southern PE Cells are not successfully controlling the external lighting. Despite confirmed voltage presence and simulation of night conditions, no switching response was observed.
No Local Time-Based Control

No C-Bus devices capable of maintaining time-based control (e.g. PAC or Application Controller with active scheduling) were found to be managing the external lighting.
The only scheduling source identified was Schedule Plus located on Level 2.
Loss of Lighting Control from Head End

Unable to gain control of external lighting via the head end PC (Schedule Plus), even after adjusting system time to force schedule activation. This indicates a breakdown in communication or execution of scheduled events.

Potential Programming / Integration Issues
It is likely that previous works may have resulted in:
Disconnection of PE Cell control wiring
Changes to group addressing
Removal or alteration of scheduling logic
Loss of integration between PE Cells and relay control groups

Network Bridge Communication Fault (High Probability)
There is a strong possibility that one or more C-Bus network bridges are:

Frozen / non-responsive
Faulty or intermittently failing

This is a known issue that can:

Prevent communication between C-Bus networks
Stop routing of control messages
Cause schedules and logic to fail across networks
Result in complete loss of control from head end systems
serviceReports.recommendations:
It is recommended to remove the existing PE Cell control of the external lighting and implement local astronomical time-based control via a C-Bus automation controller installed within the ground level lighting control boards. This will simplify the system architecture, reduce points of failure, remove reliance on network bridge communications and head end scheduling, and provide a more reliable long-term solution for control of the external lighting system.

Recommended Control Solution

Install either of the following units on the ground level lighting control boards:

Clipsal 5500PACA or 
Clipsal 5500AC2

These controllers would:

Provide local time clock and scheduling
Allow direct control of external lighting relays
Remove reliance on the head end Schedule Plus PC
Reduce dependence on network bridges for routing schedules
Improve reliability of exterior lighting operation

Due to the presence of multiple C-Bus networks separated by network bridges, it is recommended that external lighting control be localised to each network. 

This can be achieved by installing a dedicated automation controller (5500PACA or 5500AC2) within each respective board. This approach removes reliance on network bridge communication for lighting control and ensures each network can operate independently, significantly improving system reliability.

jobs.scope:
Follow-up attendance to continue fault finding and investigation of the C-Bus network wiring following replacement of failed system components, including 5 x C-Bus power supplies and 1 x 4-channel dimmer.

Works included attendance on site to investigate a suspected network short within the C-Bus field cabling. Fault-finding procedures involved isolating and tracing affected data/control cable runs throughout the property, including removal of associated switch mechanisms as required to gain access for testing purposes.

Works also included re-termination and reconnection of sensors following tracing procedures, reinstatement of all switch operation, and testing of associated switch circuits. Programming and commissioning of the newly installed dimmer for the affected lighting areas was also completed.

This invoice also includes attendance and labour associated with the electrician required to assist with fault finding and network cabling investigation works.
